questions.explain: Factory → middleware (cors() **called**, allows the 5173 origin; express.json() — without it `req.body` is undefined) → routes → **listen last**.

questions.prompt: A GET list endpoint takes `?q=&sortBy=&order=`. Which practices are correct?
options: Read from req.query · wildcards go in the VALUE (`%${q}%`) · whitelist sortBy with allowedSort.includes() — column names cannot be parameterised
Read from req.params · interpolate q into the SQL string · trust sortBy as-is
Read from req.body · use LIKE '%q%' literally · escape sortBy with quotes
Read from req.headers · use regex matching · lowercase sortBy
questions.explain: Query params live on **req.query**. Wildcards go in the parameter VALUE, never the SQL string. **Column names cannot be `?`-parameterised** → whitelist them. mysql2/promise returns `[rows, fields]` — destructure `[rows]`; DB failures → `res.status(500)`.

questions.prompt: Match the status codes: id not found · created with new id · duplicate unique key:
options: 404 · 201 with id: r.insertId · 409
400 · 200 with id: r.id · 500
410 · 201 with id: r.lastId · 401
questions.explain: Empty result for `req.params.id` → **404 Not Found**. mysql2 exposes the AUTO_INCREMENT id as **insertId** → 201 Created. Duplicate unique key (ER_DUP_ENTRY) → **409 Conflict**.

questions.prompt: After `UPDATE students SET ... WHERE id=?`, how do you detect 'id didn't exist' and what does the lab's DELETE return?
options: if (!r.affectedRows) → 404 · res.json({ deleted: true })
if (r.insertId === 0) → 400 · res.send('ok')
try/catch around the UPDATE · 204 always
Check r.changedRows === null · res.end()
questions.explain: **0 affectedRows = the id didn't exist → 404.** The WHERE id=? value is the LAST array item (req.params.id). DELETE is registered with `app.delete(path, handler)` and returns the lab's confirmation shape `{ deleted: true }` — always parameterised, always with WHERE.

AppFactory::create() builds the app → addRoutingMiddleware enables dispatch → handlers write through `getBody()` and **MUST return the response** → `run()` last (starts the middleware/dispatch lifecycle).

questions.prompt: Slim path parameters and the 201-creation pattern:
options: Params use {curly} braces (/books/{id}) arriving in array $args; 201 sets a Location: /api/books/<id> header
Params use :colon (/books/:id) arriving in $_GET; 201 needs no headers
Params use <angle> brackets; the body is in $_POST
Slim has no path params; use query strings
questions.explain: Slim uses `{id}` braces; the third callback parameter `array $args` receives them. Body comes from `getParsedBody()` (requires the JsonBodyParser middleware). **201 responses point at the new resource** with a `Location` header. `json_encode($data)` once; the helper sets header + status.

questions.prompt: In the JSON-body-parser middleware, why `$request->withParsedBody($data)` and what special method needs CORS handling?
options: PSR-7 requests are immutable — withParsedBody returns a NEW request to pass to $handler->handle(); OPTIONS preflight must be answered with 204 + headers, skipping the route
withParsedBody mutates in place; GET needs preflight
It clones the response; HEAD needs preflight
It caches the body; PUT needs preflight
questions.explain: **PSR-7 immutability**: withX() returns a NEW object — pass it on via `$handler->handle($request)`. The browser's CORS preflight is **OPTIONS** → answer 204 + headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization` — Authorization carries the JWT in Ch11). `json_decode($raw, true)` = associative array.
